meta.theme: the biological history of the century after 1492 stated at its strongest and then bounded: organisms settled the magnitudes and settled nothing about who received what, which was decided by tenure and by law, so the ecological account answers the question of how much and leaves the question of who to a different body of evidence

meta.reviewer_notes: The claim is put at its strongest before it is bounded, so the unqualified biological reading is genuinely attractive and has to be defeated by the tenure comparison rather than by hedging. The objection paragraph is written as a paragraph with a job, so that the reading which takes the objection for the thesis can be refused structurally. Three rivals, biology as the agent, ecological history as evasion, and intention as a weak unit of explanation, own one option in each of the five questions.

quality.adversarial_review: Three rivals hold an option in every question. The first, and the live one, is the claim without its qualification: organisms were the agents and human decisions the local detail. It is attractive because the first two paragraphs are written to make it as strong as possible, and it is killed by the upland comparison, where the yield is the same and the outcomes are not, and by the sentence that the difference is one of tenure and tenure is not a fact of nature. The second is the objection taken for the thesis: a history of pathogens and yields excuses the conquest, so it should be resisted. The passage answers it rather than adopting it, and the answer, the two questions take different evidence and neither substitutes for the other, makes it a paragraph with a job rather than the position of the piece. The third is the methodological generalisation that intention explains little; the passage refuses it by making tenure and law decisive at the largest scale it discusses, and by ending on somebody who marched a population to a mine. The phrase item turns on a sentence that separates the size of what must be explained from the identity of whoever acted, which is the distinction the whole argument rests on.

paragraphs.text: The most consequential things to cross the Atlantic after 1492 were not people or ideas but organisms, and most of them were invisible. Pathogens went west with the earliest ships and reduced the populations of two continents by proportions no war in the record approaches. Seeds went east: maize, the potato, cassava, the tomato, the chilli, crops that between them underwrote a century of population growth in Europe, in west Africa and in China. Cattle, pigs and horses went west and turned grassland into a kind of property it had not been before. A history of the period that leaves the biology out is not merely incomplete. It gets the quantities wrong, and the quantities are most of what happened.

This is a real gain and it is worth stating at its strongest. The biological account explains what a narrative of kings and captains cannot explain on its own: why a few hundred men could hold territory on a scale no army of that size has held before or since, and why the consequences of 1492 appear in places no European reached for another two centuries, in the upland fields of Asia and in the flour of west African villages. It changes the arithmetic and not the cast.

But the arithmetic is not the distribution, and the passage from one to the other is where the discipline lies. Biology settled what became possible. It settled nothing about who received it. Whether a new crop fed a household or paid its rent depended on who held the land it grew in; whether a shortage of hands raised wages or opened a market in people depended on what the law of the place permitted to be done to them. The same plant appears as subsistence in one valley and as an export crop in the next, and the difference between the two is never botanical. Ecology wrote the menu. Somebody else decided who ate.

Set two upland societies side by side, each of which received the sweet potato within the same half-century and got much the same yield from it. In the first, households grew it on ground they could pass to their children, and the population rose and was fed. In the second, the surplus it produced was taken as rent, and the same yield left hunger behind it and a larger quantity for export. The contribution of the plant was identical in both. The difference was one of tenure, and tenure is not a fact of nature.

There is an objection to this kind of history that deserves an answer rather than a shrug. An account that explains a catastrophe in pathogens and yields, with nobody's name in it, can be heard as an excuse: if most of the deaths were biological, the conquest becomes a misfortune. The answer is that the two questions take different evidence and that neither stands in for the other. How much requires burial grounds, tallies, yields and prices. Who did what requires orders, contracts, ledgers and the records of courts. The pathogens explain the size of the collapse and say nothing at all about who marched a population to a mine, and a historian who runs the two together has stopped doing either.

questions.target_mistake: keeping the claim of the first two paragraphs without the boundary the rest of the passage draws around it
questions.prediction_target: Before the options the learner should be able to say: the biological account is necessary for the magnitudes and silent about the distribution, so the passage needs both halves and subordinates neither.
questions.stem: Which of the following best states the main idea of the passage?

options.A: The decisive agents after 1492 were organisms rather than people, and the political story, though not false, is a local detail of a biological event.
options.B: Biology explains the scale of what followed 1492 and not its distribution, which was settled by tenure and by law, so both accounts are required.
options.C: A history told in pathogens and yields is an evasion, because it explains a catastrophe without requiring anybody at all to answer for it.
options.D: Historians overrate intention: the largest changes were produced by forces nobody chose, even where the record preserves the names of those who acted.

explanation.expert_notice: The hinge is the first sentence of the third paragraph: 'But the arithmetic is not the distribution, and the passage from one to the other is where the discipline lies.' Everything before it makes the biological case as strong as possible, and everything after it says what that case does not reach.
explanation.correct_reasoning: The correct option keeps both parts and their relation. Biology is granted the magnitudes without reservation, and then denied any authority over who received what, which the passage assigns to tenure and to law. The upland comparison and the closing division of evidence both exist to keep that boundary in view, and only a statement that carries the boundary explains why the passage does not stop after its second paragraph.
explanation.question_type_note: In a claim-and-qualification passage the main idea is the claim together with its limit. An option carrying only the claim will match the opening paragraphs exactly, which is what makes it dangerous.
explanation.reading_habit: Find the sentence beginning with 'but' that separates the two halves of the argument, and check that your candidate main idea contains material from both sides of it.

distractors.why_wrong: This is the claim as the first two paragraphs state it, before the limit is imposed. The upland comparison then holds the plant and the yield constant and finds two different outcomes, and the passage says the difference 'was one of tenure, and tenure is not a fact of nature'.
distractors.seductive_element: The opening is written at full strength and without hedging, so a reader who fixes the main idea early will find it confirmed by every example in the first half.

distractors.why_wrong: This is the objection the last paragraph is written to answer, not the position it reaches. The answer given is that the two questions take different evidence and neither stands in for the other, which defends the ecological account while refusing to let it settle responsibility.
distractors.seductive_element: The objection is stated with real force and in the author's own voice, and a reader who meets it late may take the final paragraph for the conclusion rather than the reply.

distractors.why_wrong: The passage argues about one period and makes human arrangements decisive within it: who held the land, what the law permitted, who was marched to a mine. A general demotion of intention would leave the third and fourth paragraphs pointing the wrong way.
distractors.seductive_element: Histories built on organisms usually come with a methodological moral attached, and the first paragraph's scale invites one.

questions.target_mistake: hearing the phrase as a verdict on the importance of human actors rather than as a statement about which part of the account the biology revises
questions.prediction_target: Before the options the learner should be able to say: the phrase is summing up a paragraph about magnitudes, so it must be saying that the size of the thing changes while the question of who acted does not.
questions.stem: The phrase “It changes the arithmetic and not the cast” conveys that the biological account

options.A: alters the size of what has to be explained while leaving the question of who acted where it was
options.B: shows that the organisms in this history mattered a great deal more than any of the people involved did
options.C: takes the actors out of a history in which their names ought to have been recorded and kept
options.D: replaces the study of what people intended with the study of the forces that acted upon them

explanation.expert_notice: The sentence closes a paragraph about quantities: the scale of territory held, the reach of consequences into places no European visited. The word arithmetic points back to those magnitudes, and the following paragraph opens by naming the thing the arithmetic does not settle.
explanation.correct_reasoning: The correct option keeps both halves of the phrase in their places. What the biology revises is how large the thing to be explained is; what it leaves untouched is the cast, which the next paragraph immediately puts to work deciding who received the new calories and under what law. Read this way the sentence is a hinge, and the passage's whole second half follows from it.
explanation.question_type_note: A phrase question is settled by the work the phrase does where it sits. A sentence that ends one paragraph and sets up the next has to be read against both.
explanation.reading_habit: When an author coins a two-part phrase, check what each part refers to in the surrounding sentences. Options that keep the phrase's music while changing its referents are the standard trap.

distractors.why_wrong: The phrase says the cast is unchanged, not that it is diminished. The passage then spends two paragraphs making human arrangements decisive, and its closing sentence insists that the pathogens say nothing at all about who marched a population to a mine.
distractors.seductive_element: The first paragraph really does subordinate people to organisms in the matter of scale, so a reader arrives at the phrase already ranking the two.

distractors.why_wrong: Removing the actors is the complaint the final paragraph answers, and this phrase is where the author denies it in advance by keeping the cast intact. Taking the sentence as a confession reverses the direction of the argument at its hinge.
distractors.seductive_element: The objection is real and is stated in the passage, so its vocabulary is available and feels like the author's own.

distractors.why_wrong: A replacement of one study by another is a claim about how history should be done, and the phrase is a claim about one account's effect on one body of evidence. The passage ends by insisting that both studies are needed and that each has its own documents.
distractors.seductive_element: Arithmetic against cast sounds like a contrast between impersonal forces and human motives, which is the shape of a familiar methodological quarrel.

questions.target_mistake: widening the argument into a general position about historical explanation, or narrowing it into the objection the last paragraph answers
questions.prediction_target: Before the options the learner should be able to say: the account is offered for one question, how much changed, and is explicitly said not to settle the second, who received what.
questions.stem: The account the author defends is best described as an account of

options.A: what happened after 1492, in which human decisions figure as the local detail of a biological process
options.B: the risks run by any history that explains a great change without naming a single person in it
options.C: the general weakness of intention as a unit for explaining change on the largest historical scale
options.D: how much changed after 1492, which must be completed by a separate account of how it was shared out

explanation.expert_notice: The third paragraph states the boundary in two short sentences: 'Biology settled what became possible. It settled nothing about who received it', and the last paragraph gives each question its own evidence: burial grounds and yields for one, orders and contracts for the other.
explanation.correct_reasoning: The correct option names that division of labour. The passage claims the magnitudes for biology, insists that the distribution belongs elsewhere, and treats the second account as necessary rather than optional, which is why the upland comparison and the final list of documents are in the passage at all. An option that claims more or less than this leaves one of those paragraphs unexplained.
explanation.question_type_note: Scope questions ask how far a claim reaches. Look for the sentences where the author says what the claim does not cover, and make sure your option reproduces the boundary rather than the enthusiasm.
explanation.reading_habit: State any argument as the question it answers. Wrong options are usually answers to a bigger question or to an objection the author merely handled along the way.

distractors.why_wrong: The passage refuses to make decisions a detail of the process: whether a crop fed a household or paid its rent depended on who held the land, and the upland pair differ in outcome with the plant held constant. The first two paragraphs are the claim at full strength, not its final extent.
distractors.seductive_element: It is a fair description of the opening, which is deliberately written without qualification so that the limit arrives as a surprise.

distractors.why_wrong: This names the objection the final paragraph takes up, not the account being defended. The author answers it by separating two questions and keeping both, which would be an odd thing to do in an essay whose subject was the danger of the first.
distractors.seductive_element: The last paragraph is the most forceful in the passage, and readers often take a closing argument for the thesis regardless of what it is arguing against.

distractors.why_wrong: The passage makes intention decisive exactly where it matters most, in the law that permitted a market in people and the tenure that turned a surplus into rent. Its claims are about one period and one body of evidence, and no general thesis about historical explanation is argued for.
distractors.seductive_element: The scale of the opening invites a methodological moral, and readers expect essays of this kind to end in one.

questions.target_mistake: reading the comparison as evidence of how far the new crops spread, or as a demonstration that like causes produce like effects
questions.prediction_target: The learner should be able to say beforehand: the two cases are matched on the biology so that the only thing left to explain the difference is the arrangement of holdings.
questions.stem: The pair of upland societies in the fourth paragraph serves chiefly to

options.A: illustrate how far the new crops spread beyond any territory a European army ever reached
options.B: show what a history of magnitudes loses when it leaves out the people who made decisions
options.C: demonstrate that similar forces will produce similar outcomes wherever they happen to operate
options.D: hold the plant and the yield constant so that the difference made by tenure becomes visible

explanation.expert_notice: The paragraph is built as a matched pair. The crop is the same, the half-century is the same, and the yield is 'much the same'; only the holding of the ground differs. The last sentence names the variable that is left: 'The difference was one of tenure, and tenure is not a fact of nature.'
explanation.correct_reasoning: The correct option describes that construction. By equalising the biology the author removes it as an explanation of the outcomes, so whatever separates the two societies has to come from somewhere else, and the paragraph names it. The example is therefore doing argumentative work for the qualification introduced one paragraph earlier rather than adding a further illustration of reach.
explanation.question_type_note: Role-of-detail questions ask what a passage would lose without the detail. A matched pair almost always exists to hold one variable still.
explanation.reading_habit: When an author gives two cases that agree in every respect but one, read for the respect in which they differ. That difference is the claim the example was built to carry.

distractors.why_wrong: The reach of the crops is established in the previous paragraph, with the upland fields of Asia and the flour of west African villages. This paragraph is about two places that both received the plant and diverged, which is a point about outcomes rather than about distance.
distractors.seductive_element: Uplands have just been mentioned as evidence of spread, so the reader arrives at the paragraph with that function already in mind.

distractors.why_wrong: The complaint about histories without people belongs to the final paragraph and is there to be answered. Here nobody is missing from the account; the paragraph supplies a specific institutional difference and shows it doing the work the biology cannot do.
distractors.seductive_element: The example does bring human arrangements back into a story about seeds, which is easily heard as the moral complaint rather than the analytical one.

distractors.why_wrong: The pair shows the reverse: the same plant, the same yield and the same half-century produce a fed population in one case and hunger with a larger export in the other. If like forces produced like outcomes the paragraph would refute the passage's own qualification.
distractors.seductive_element: Matched examples are often used to establish regularity, and a reader who registers the matching without reading the outcomes will assume that is what is happening.

questions.target_mistake: inferring a consequence for people from a change in the quantity of food, which is exactly the step the passage's qualification forbids
questions.prediction_target: Before the options the learner should be able to say: a crop fixes what is available and not who gets it, so identical biology is compatible with opposite outcomes.
questions.stem: Which of the following can be inferred from the passage?

options.A: Two societies that received the same crop at the same time could diverge for reasons the crop cannot explain.
options.B: Where a new crop increased the quantity of food grown, the people who grew it were in consequence better fed.
options.C: A history written in burial counts and yields leaves its reader with no way of assigning responsibility.
options.D: The larger the change a historian has to explain, the less that human intention can contribute to explaining it.

explanation.expert_notice: The fourth paragraph is the inference already performed once: same plant, same yield, same half-century, opposite outcomes, with tenure named as the difference. The third paragraph states the principle behind it in two sentences about what biology settles and what it does not.
explanation.correct_reasoning: The correct option generalises the matched pair by one step. If the biological contribution can be identical while the outcomes differ, then the crop cannot be what explains the divergence, and the explanation has to be sought in the arrangements the passage names: who held the ground, and what the law allowed. Nothing stronger is asserted, which is why it survives the passage's own restrictions.
explanation.question_type_note: When a passage supplies a controlled comparison, the safest inference is the one that states what the control rules out. Options that reinstate the ruled-out cause are the standard trap.
explanation.reading_habit: After reading a matched example, say aloud what it proves cannot be the explanation. Half the wrong options in such a set will be that explanation in other clothes.

distractors.why_wrong: This is the step the passage exists to block. Whether a new crop fed a household or paid its rent depended on who held the land, and in the second upland case the same yield left hunger behind it and a larger quantity for export.
distractors.seductive_element: More food ought to mean better fed, and the first paragraph's talk of crops underwriting population growth appears to license the move.

distractors.why_wrong: The passage says the second question needs different evidence, not that it cannot be answered: orders, contracts, ledgers and the records of courts are named for it. What it denies is that an answer about magnitude doubles as an answer about responsibility.
distractors.seductive_element: It is the near-tie, since the author agrees that a history of yields contains nobody's name, and a reader may take the diagnosis for the verdict.

distractors.why_wrong: At the largest scale the passage discusses, the decisive variables are still tenure and law, and the closing sentence puts a named human act beside the biggest quantity in the piece. The size of a change is never offered as a measure of how much intention explains.
distractors.seductive_element: The opening paragraph really does make the largest effects biological, which suggests a rule of proportion the passage never states.

mentor.challenge: The first half of this passage makes a case as strongly as it can be made. Read the second half for the boundary the author then draws around it, and notice that the boundary is the argument.
mentor.one_sentence_summary: The organisms that crossed the Atlantic after 1492 explain the scale of what followed and nothing about its distribution, which was decided by who held the land and what the law permitted, so the ecological account answers one question and leaves a second to different evidence.
mentor.main_idea: Pathogens, crops and livestock account for magnitudes that no narrative of kings and captains can reach. But biology settles only what becomes possible. Who was fed, who paid rent and who was forced to work was settled by tenure and by law. The two questions need different documents, and answering the first has never answered the second.
mentor.simple_explanation:
After 1492 the most important travellers across the Atlantic were not people. They were germs, seeds and animals. Diseases went west and killed people on a scale no war matches. Crops went east, maize, potatoes, cassava, and fed huge population growth in Europe, Africa and China. Cattle and horses went west and changed what land was used for.

So any history that ignores biology gets the numbers badly wrong, and the numbers are most of the story.

Then comes the turn. Biology decides what becomes possible. It does not decide who gets it. Whether a new crop fed a family or was taken as rent depended on who owned the land. Whether a shortage of workers meant higher wages or slavery depended on what the law allowed.

The author gives a clean comparison. Two upland societies get the sweet potato at about the same time and get about the same harvest from it. In one, families own the land, and the population grows and eats. In the other, the extra harvest is taken as rent, so the same crop leaves hunger and more exports. The plant did the same thing in both. The difference was ownership, and ownership is not natural.

Finally the author answers an objection. If the deaths were mostly caused by disease, does that let the conquerors off? No: the two questions use different evidence. How many died is answered by graves, harvest records and prices. Who did what is answered by orders, contracts and court records. Germs explain the size of the disaster. They say nothing about who marched people into a mine.
mentor.why_difficult: The passage is written so that its first half is a complete and attractive argument on its own, and a reader who settles there will find matching options everywhere. The qualification arrives as a distinction between two words that sound similar in this context, the arithmetic and the distribution, and the reader has to keep them apart for three paragraphs. The final paragraph then states a forceful objection in the author's own voice and answers it, which readers regularly mistake for the conclusion.
mentor.author_intention: To keep a powerful kind of explanation from being asked to do a job it cannot do, without giving up any of the ground it has genuinely won.

paragraph_journey.note: Germs, seeds and animals crossing the Atlantic changed populations and diets at a scale no political story can reach.
It explains why tiny forces held huge territories and why the effects show up where no European ever went. It changes the size, not the cast.
Biology fixed what was possible and nothing about who received it. Land holding and law decided whether a crop fed people or paid rent.
Same crop, same yield, same period, opposite outcomes. The difference was who owned the ground.
Explaining a catastrophe in germs is not an excuse for anyone, because the question of who acted needs its own documents.

mentor.tone_progression: Expansive and confident while the biological case is built, sharper at the pivot where the claim is bounded, controlled and specific through the comparison, and firm at the end, where an objection is taken seriously and refused.
key_transitions: 'It changes the arithmetic and not the cast.' (paragraph 2): the hinge between the two halves of the argument.
'But the arithmetic is not the distribution' (paragraph 3): the qualification the whole passage exists to make.
'There is an objection to this kind of history that deserves an answer rather than a shrug.' (paragraph 5): the objection is engaged rather than adopted.
mentor.misunderstanding: Two misreadings are common and both are built from real paragraphs. The first takes the opening as the whole thesis, so that organisms become the agents of the period and people become scenery; the upland pair is written to stop it, since the plant is held constant and the outcomes are not. The second takes the closing objection for the author's position, so that ecological history becomes an evasion; but the paragraph answers the objection by dividing the evidence, which is a defence of the account rather than a retreat from it.
mentor.traps_summary: The options in this set are built from the claim without its limit, from the objection the author answers, and from a general methodological moral the author never draws. Each is close to something the passage says. When a passage states a claim at full strength and then bounds it, expect the unbounded version to be the most attractive wrong answer in every question.
mentor.reading_lesson: When an author spends two paragraphs making a case as strong as possible, read on for the sentence that says what the case does not settle. Strong statements of that kind are nearly always set-ups for a boundary, and the boundary is where the questions live. Holding the two halves apart, and being able to say which question each answers, is what separates a reader who can use such a passage from one who merely agrees with it.
mentor.real_world: The same discipline is needed whenever a structural explanation meets a question about conduct: in arguments about poverty, epidemics and climate, an account of the magnitudes is routinely offered as though it settled who was responsible for the distribution.
mentor.takeaway: An explanation of how much changed is never by itself an answer to who decided.
mentor.reflection_question: When you next hear a large problem explained by forces nobody chose, what would you need to see before deciding that nobody chose anything?
